audit.whatIsWrong: Early phase said Sanguine Pool 'is on a long early cooldown' without ever giving the number.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16. Twenty-eight seconds at rank 1 is the single largest window either champion has in this lane, and 'long' does not tell you whether to commit now or wait.
audit.corrected: Every pool reference now carries 28s at rank 1, and the level 3, level 6 and first-item spikes are keyed to it.

audit.why: The level 3 / level 6 / first-item / two-item shape is right: your burst outruns his heals before Rylai's and Liandry's, and the Crimson Pact health-from-AP conversion is what flips it after.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood was described as 'ground poke' that 'charges up before it detonates', with nothing about minions.
audit.why: Riot's text: he pays his own health to charge a reservoir which, when released, deals damage in the area AROUND HIM — and it can be blocked by enemy units. Standing behind your own wave removes the poke entirely, which is the strongest early counterplay in the lane and was missing.
audit.corrected: E now described as bursting around him and body-blocked by minions, with the instruction to trade from behind your wave.

edits.before: With Q, E and your Assassin's Mark passive online you win the short trade — E-in across your energy ring for the empowered auto and Q, then back off before his Transfusion (Q) heal stacks. Punish hardest when his W pool is on cooldown.
edits.after: With Q, E and your Assassin's Mark passive online you win the short trade — E-in across your energy ring for the empowered auto and Q, then back off before his Transfusion (Q) heal stacks. Punish hardest when Sanguine Pool is down, 28s at rank 1.

edits.before: R is a gap-closer plus a missing-HP finisher — cast one dashes through him, cast two re-dashes for execute damage scaling on how low he is. His best counter is pooling (W) at the cast-one moment to go untargetable, so bait the pool with Shroud first.
edits.after: R is a gap-closer plus a missing-HP finisher — cast one dashes through him, cast two re-dashes for execute damage scaling on how low he is. His best counter is pooling (W) at the cast-one moment to go untargetable, so bait that 28s pool with Shroud first.

edits.before: Force out Sanguine Pool (W) with Shroud or your E-dash, then chain R while he can't pool away your re-dash and go untargetable
edits.after: Force out Sanguine Pool (W) with Shroud or your E-dash, then chain R inside the 28s window while he cannot go untargetable

edits.before: Drop Twilight Shroud to go untargetable through his E (Tides of Blood) poke and reset the trade when he tries to drain back with Q
edits.after: Trade from behind your own wave — his E (Tides of Blood) bursts around him and enemy units body-block it, so minions eat the poke for you

edits.before: Stack Transfusion (Q) heals and E poke from max range to grind down your energy-gated, all-in trades
edits.after: Stack Transfusion (Q) heals, empowered when his resource is full, to grind down your energy-gated trades

edits.before: Both of you are weak at level 1 — Vlad has one of the worst early laning phases in the game, but you only have Q (Five Point Strike) with no Shroud or sustain yet, so don't force a fight. Deny his Transfusion (Q) last-hits with your kunai range and sidestep his E (Tides of Blood) — that ground poke charges up before it detonates, so walk out of the wind-up instead of eating it. He has no dash escape and his Sanguine Pool (W) is on a long early cooldown, so once you hit 3 with your Assassin's Mark passive running you can punish a greedy E with a quick E-in trade.
edits.after: Both of you are weak at level 1 — Vlad has one of the worst early laning phases in the game, but you only have Q (Five Point Strike) with no Shroud or sustain yet, so don't force a fight. Deny his Transfusion (Q) last-hits with your kunai range and note where his E (Tides of Blood) lands: it bursts in the area around HIM and enemy units block it outright, so standing behind your own wave deletes the poke. He has no dash escape and Sanguine Pool (W) is 28s at rank 1, so once you hit 3 with Assassin's Mark running you can punish a greedy E.

edits.before: This is your window. Your combo bursts a pre-Rylai Vlad faster than his Transfusion (Q) and Sanguine Pool (W) heals can stabilize him — so spend Shroud or your E to force the pool first, because once W is on its long cooldown he's far more killable. At 6, R turns every step-up lethal: E-in, drop Shroud to break his E poke and bait the pool, then commit R — cast one through him, cast two re-dashing for the missing-HP execute. Just don't whiff E into nothing; without that mark-and-dash you have no all-in and he simply drains the trade back.
edits.after: This is your window. Your combo bursts a pre-Rylai Vlad faster than his Transfusion (Q) and Sanguine Pool (W) heals can stabilize him — so spend Shroud or your E to force the pool first, because on a 28s rank-1 cooldown he is far more killable for the rest of it. At 6, R turns every step-up lethal: E-in, drop Shroud to break his E poke and bait the pool, then commit R — cast one through him, cast two re-dashing for the missing-HP execute. Just don't whiff E into nothing; without the mark you have no all-in.

edits.before: He still has no dash and you have no Shroud, so trade carefully with Q range and sidestep his E poke as it charges — it's genuinely even at 2.
edits.after: He still has no dash and you have no Shroud, so trade at Q range and stand behind minions, which body-block his Tides of Blood entirely.

edits.before: Shroud lets you reset trades and dodge his E poke, but a Transfusion-healing Vlad out-sustains your energy-gated rotation — it's genuinely even here.
edits.after: Shroud lets you reset trades and your own minions block his E, but a Transfusion-healing Vlad out-sustains your energy-gated rotation — even here.

edits.before: R is a gap-closer plus a missing-HP execute — bait the pool with Shroud, then commit cast one and re-dash cast two before he can go untargetable.
edits.after: R is a gap-closer plus a missing-HP execute — bait the 28s pool with Shroud, then commit cast one and re-dash before he goes untargetable.

edits.before: Bully him early — build MR, shroud his pool window. Akali wins the Sanguine Pool cooldown windows.
edits.after: Bully him early — build MR and bait the 28s pool. Akali wins the Sanguine Pool cooldown windows.

edits.before: Shroud rewrites any trade he starts. Only take the trade when Vladimir's Sanguine Pool is down.
edits.after: Shroud rewrites any trade he starts. Take it when Sanguine Pool is down, 28s at rank 1.

edits.before: Dodges your burst. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It goes untargetable, 28s at rank 1. Bait it before you commit R.

notes: The strongest early counterplay in this lane was missing entirely: Tides of Blood can be blocked by enemy units, so trading from behind your own wave removes his only pre-6 poke. The old text described it as a ground zone that 'charges up before it detonates' — it detonates around Vladimir himself. Sanguine Pool's 28s rank-1 cooldown was never stated despite the whole matchup being written around baiting it.
